REFLECTION.signature: U_info encodes PAIRED-INTRON CONSISTENCY and DONOR-IDENTITY CONFIDENCE. The coupling is partner-specific ~37x (partner +0.966 [0.827,1.107] vs distance-matched non-partner AG +0.026 [0.009,0.045]) and donor-specific ~74x (donor +0.964 vs non-site masked G +0.013 [-0.006,0.036]); it is strand-symmetric (+1.067 vs -0.848, overlapping CIs); and it is FLAT across intron length mod 3 (0/1/2 = 1.052/0.835/0.985, heavily overlapping).
REFLECTION.interpretation: This matches the prompt's most-defensible MLM reading: a donor-like GT becomes more probable when its SPECIFIC paired acceptor is intact -- the circuit distinguishes a genuine donor boundary from an incidental GT, conditioned on the partner. It is NOT generic splice-site evidence (non-partner ~0), NOT a global G shift (non-site G ~0), and NOT raw cross-site phase alignment (no intron-mod-3 dependence, consistent with SpliceBERT processing unspliced RNA where intron length mod 3 is arbitrary).

intent_check.summary: The annotation-free core resolves U_info's identity: partner-specificity + donor-specificity together pin it as paired-intron-consistency / donor-identity, and the deferred conditions are refinements, not load-bearing for this core reading. 1e turns the structural graph (1a-1c) into a mechanistic explanation of what flows.
intent_check.deferred: Coding-vs-noncoding (dataset is protein-coding-only; needs a rebuild including noncoding transcripts) and ANNOTATED splice phase 0/1/2 (needs CDS-frame annotation). Both are built in the period-3 bridge and applied back to complete the signature; the 'phase-sensitive boundary' hypothesis stays OPEN until annotated phase is tested. The intron-mod-3 flatness bears only on RAW cross-site alignment, not biological boundary phase.

checked: S-Partner uses a DISTANCE-MATCHED non-partner AG (matched_decoy_acceptor), so partner-specificity is not confounded with attention distance-decay; it could have matched the partner (generic) and did not (~37x apart).
S-Donor's non-site G is >=30 nt from both sites; the corruption could have shifted it (global G effect) and did not (~0), so the readout is donor-specific.
S-Strand: the effect is present and overlapping on both strands, ruling out the kind of strand-handling bug that made the pre-R11 study plus-strand-only.
Same native readout and unconditional set as C16-C18; partner coupling +0.966 matches the known unconditional val coupling.
escaped_failure_modes.residual_risk: The signature is measured on the COUPLING; it inherits (via C16 C-Suff) that the coupling is what U_info carries, rather than re-routing each condition through U_info -- a reasonable economy, but a per-condition U_info-routing check would tighten the 'U_info specifically' claim. Period-3 dependence is cited (C8), not re-measured here.
